chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

It is recommended that a wet twig be inserted with him in his grave, and his grave be raised from the ground by the measure of four clenched fingers, and water be sprinkled upon it, and he be left alone.

key_terms.أَرْبَعِ أَصَابِعَ مَضْمُومَةٍ: Four clenched fingers (a traditional unit of measurement for height)
key_terms.يُسْتَحَبُّ: It is recommended (a legal ruling indicating preference but not obligation)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended practices for preparing and raising a grave according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the Sunnah of grave preparation, emphasizing the placement of a fresh palm frond (jarīdah) to symbolize freshness and the raising of the grave mound by four finger-widths to distinguish it from the ground. These practices reflect the Shia tradition of honoring the deceased with dignity and simplicity, ensuring the grave is marked yet not overly elevated, while sprinkling water serves to settle the earth and provide a cooling effect.
